dossier.title: Two responses. A clearer decision.
dossier.subtitle: Compare the answer, understand the tradeoffs, and decide what to try next. An example with illustrative data.

pages.title: Responses
pages.summary: Same task, two approaches. Compare how each response answers the brief.

blocks.prompt: Turn release notes about saved views, CSV export and faster search into a brief for a product manager. Explain what changed, who benefits, and one next step.

left.label: Response A
left.caption: Baseline prompt · broad summary
left.value:
The latest release includes several improvements to help users work more efficiently. Saved views make the experience more flexible, CSV export helps with reporting, and search is now faster.

These changes should benefit teams across the organization by improving productivity and making information easier to access.

We recommend exploring the new features and gathering feedback to understand their impact.

right.label: Response B
right.caption: Revised prompt · explicit structure
right.value:
What changed: Teams can save a filtered view, export its results to CSV, and search the same workspace more quickly.

Who benefits: Operations teams can reuse their weekly review view. Analysts can take a result set into a spreadsheet without copying rows by hand.

Next step: Ask one operations team to use a saved view for its next weekly review. Record setup time and any missing filters before expanding the rollout.

blocks.note: B gives the reviewer a concrete audience and a testable next step. Highlighting shows wording changes; it does not determine which answer is better.

blocks.title: Test the revised prompt on a broader sample
blocks.context: The example favors the structured response, especially for clarity and actionability. One task cannot show how either approach handles other inputs.
blocks.decision: Use B as the candidate for the next evaluation, keeping A as the baseline.
blocks.consequences: This adds review time and a risk of overfitting the prompt to a narrow task. Keep the same rubric and include cases where a longer answer is necessary.

items.label: Set the baseline
items.detail: Choose 20 representative prompts and freeze the rubric.

items.label: Run both variants
items.detail: Keep model settings and input context identical. Record latency, tokens and failures.

items.label: Review and decide
items.detail: Score responses without showing the variant label. Record disagreements and repeat uncertain cases.
